plays.story: D&D: Honor Among Thieves sequel script is finished and Hasbro/eOne are shopping for a studio to make it

angles.bizzal-games: 'The Sequel Script Is Done — Here's What a Green-Lit Honor Among Thieves 2 Means for Your Table': break down what a studio-shopped script means for the D&D brand's momentum, tie-in product timing, and whether a movie deal could reshape 5.5E/VTT marketing pushes.
angles.itsalreadywritten: 'They Finished the Script Before They Found a Studio — What That Says About How D&D Stories Get Told': use the stalled greenlight as a hook to dissect what made the first film's narrative work (found-family heist structure) and what a sequel script has to solve narratively to top it.

plays.story: Netflix moves forward on a Ravenloft series while the Forgotten Realms TV series is confirmed dead

angles.bizzal-games: 'Netflix Just Told Wizards Which D&D IP Sells: Gothic Horror, Not Core Setting' — analyze the business signal behind killing the flagship Forgotten Realms show in favor of Ravenloft, and what it means for which settings get licensing dollars next.
angles.itsalreadywritten: 'Ravenloft Already Wrote Netflix's Show For Them: A Curse of Strahd Adaptation Primer' — walk through how decades of Ravenloft modules (I6, Curse of Strahd) already contain the arcs, villains, and set pieces a showrunner would need, and where the source material could trip up a TV adaptation.

plays.story: Trezor discloses a second wave of breach notifications (67K US customers) tied to third-party vendor ShipMonk

angles.itsalreadypriced: 'Trezor's Breach Keeps Growing — Here's What Self-Custody Users Should Actually Do' — cover the phishing/mail-scam risk this creates for hardware wallet holders and what it means for trust in cold storage vendors amid a bull market.
angles.itsalreadywhen: 'One Vendor, Two Breaches: The ShipMonk Incident Is a Supply-Chain Case Study' — dig into how a single fulfillment/logistics vendor compromise re-surfaced months later, and what third-party risk lessons security teams should take from Trezor's repeat disclosure.

plays.story: The Coldcard hardware-wallet hacker launders stolen Bitcoin into ETH via THORChain

angles.itsalreadypriced: 'Stolen Bitcoin Just Went Through THORChain — What That Means for On-Chain Tracing' — explain the cross-chain laundering trend, why THORChain keeps showing up in hacks, and what it signals for exchange/compliance risk.
angles.itsalreadywhen: 'How a Hardware Wallet Hack Becomes an Untraceable Payday: Inside the Coldcard-to-THORChain Playbook' — break down the technical laundering chain as a case study in post-breach threat-actor tradecraft and cross-chain bridge exploitation.
